job_description:
Data Scientist - Machine Learning

We're looking for a talented Data Scientist to help us leverage data for business insights.

Requirements:
• Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, or related field
• 3+ years of experience in data science or machine learning
• Strong programming skills in Python (NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn)
• Experience with deep learning frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch)
• Knowledge of statistical analysis and A/B testing
• Experience with SQL and big data technologies

Responsibilities:
• Build and deploy machine learning models
• Analyze large datasets to extract insights
• Collaborate with engineering to productionize models
• Present findings to stakeholders
• Stay current with ML/AI advancements

competencies.name: Machine Learning Model Development
competencies.rationale: Given the responsibility to build and deploy machine learning models, a deep understanding of debugging is essential to identify and resolve issues in model performance, data pipelines, and training processes. This ensures robust and reliable model development cycles.

competencies.name: Large-Scale Data Analysis and Insight Extraction
competencies.rationale: The role involves analyzing large datasets to extract actionable business insights. The data insight style enables candidates to demonstrate their ability to interpret complex data patterns, perform statistical analysis, and communicate findings effectively to stakeholders.

competencies.name: Model Production and Integration with Engineering
competencies.rationale: Collaboration with engineering to productionize models requires understanding of system design and scalability. The system design scaling style ensures candidates can discuss how models are integrated into production systems, monitored, and maintained at scale.

criteria.name: Debugging Model Performance and Data Pipelines
criteria.description: Ability to identify and resolve issues in model training, data preprocessing, and feature engineering that impact performance and reliability.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Fails to identify or resolve errors; model performance degrades without intervention; no logs or error tracking.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Can identify basic errors in code or data; uses logging and basic debugging tools; limited impact on model output.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Systematically debugs model performance issues; uses profiling and error tracing; identifies data drift or pipeline bugs.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Proactively identifies and resolves complex model failures; uses A/B testing and model monitoring tools to validate fixes.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Diagnoses and resolves edge-case failures in distributed or large-scale environments; implements automated error detection and alerting.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Anticipates and prevents model failures through proactive monitoring, anomaly detection, and robust error handling in production.

criteria.name: Proficiency with Deep Learning Frameworks
criteria.description: Demonstrated ability to implement and tune deep learning models using TensorFlow, PyTorch, or equivalent frameworks.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Does not use deep learning frameworks; relies on basic statistical methods only; no implementation of neural networks.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Can implement simple neural networks with basic layers; limited customization and no optimization.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Implements and trains standard architectures (e.g., CNN, RNN); tunes hyperparameters with basic optimization techniques.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Builds and optimizes complex models (e.g., attention-based, transformer models); uses gradient clipping, batch normalization.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Designs and deploys custom architectures for domain-specific tasks; integrates with distributed training frameworks.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Innovates model architecture to improve performance; applies advanced techniques like mixed precision, quantization, and pruning.

criteria.name: Model Evaluation and Validation
criteria.description: Ability to select, apply, and interpret appropriate evaluation metrics (e.g., precision, recall, F1, AUC) in context of business goals.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Uses only basic metrics without context; fails to interpret or report results meaningfully.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Applies common metrics but does not interpret them in business context; lacks validation strategy.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Selects and applies relevant metrics; validates results with cross-validation and baseline comparisons.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Critically evaluates model performance across domains; considers bias, fairness, and data drift.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Uses multi-metric evaluation and interprets results for stakeholders; justifies model selection based on business impact.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Designs custom evaluation frameworks for novel use cases; integrates model performance with real-world KPIs.

evaluation_criteria.category: Large-Scale Data Analysis and Insight Extraction

criteria.name: Pattern Recognition in Complex Datasets
criteria.description: Ability to identify meaningful patterns, anomalies, and trends in large-scale, multi-dimensional datasets.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Fails to detect patterns; relies on manual inspection; no automated analysis tools used.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Can identify simple trends in small datasets; uses basic visualization tools (e.g., histograms, scatter plots).
scoring_levels.Level 2: Detects and visualizes complex patterns using statistical methods and data exploration tools (e.g., PCA, clustering).
scoring_levels.Level 3: Applies domain-specific techniques (e.g., time-series analysis, segmentation) to extract actionable insights.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Uses advanced analytics (e.g., dimensionality reduction, feature engineering) to uncover hidden relationships.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Develops automated data exploration pipelines that surface insights without human intervention.

criteria.name: Statistical Analysis and A/B Testing
criteria.description: Demonstrated ability to apply statistical methods and conduct A/B testing to validate product or model effectiveness.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Does not apply statistical methods; no understanding of hypothesis testing or confidence intervals.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Conducts basic A/B tests with limited statistical rigor; does not interpret p-values or effect sizes.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Designs and executes A/B tests with appropriate sample size and controls; interprets results with confidence intervals.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Applies advanced statistical models (e.g., multivariate testing, power analysis) to assess impact.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Designs experiments with real-world business impact; accounts for confounding variables and external factors.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Designs and scales randomized experiments for large user bases; uses Bayesian methods and sequential testing.

criteria.name: Translating Data into Stakeholder Insights
criteria.description: Ability to present complex data findings in clear, actionable, and non-technical language to stakeholders.

scoring_levels.Level 0: Fails to communicate findings; reports raw data without interpretation or context.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Summarizes data in simple terms; lacks visual or narrative support for key insights.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Uses visualizations and summaries to explain patterns; explains implications to non-technical audiences.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Tailors insights to different stakeholder needs; connects data to business outcomes.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Anticipates stakeholder questions and provides data-backed recommendations with risk assessment.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Designs data storytelling frameworks that drive decision-making and influence strategy.

evaluation_criteria.category: Model Production and Integration with Engineering

criteria.name: End-to-End Model Deployment Pipeline
criteria.description: Ability to design and implement scalable, automated pipelines for model training, validation, and deployment.

scoring_levels.Level 0: No pipeline; manual model deployment with no automation or versioning.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Uses basic scripts for model deployment; no monitoring or rollback mechanisms.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Implements CI/CD pipeline with basic model versioning (e.g., MLflow); limited monitoring.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Designs and deploys automated, repeatable pipelines with error handling and logging.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Integrates model lifecycle with cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS SageMaker, GCP); supports A/B testing in production.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Builds self-healing, self-monitoring pipelines with automated alerts and rollback on failure.

criteria.name: Scalability and System Design for Production Models
criteria.description: Understanding of system design principles to support model performance at scale and under load.

scoring_levels.Level 0: No understanding of scalability; models run on single machines with no load handling.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Can deploy models on a single server; no load balancing or failover.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Implements basic load balancing and containerization (e.g., Docker); uses Kubernetes for orchestration.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Designs scalable model serving with batching and caching strategies; handles peak loads.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Optimizes model latency and throughput using batching, model pruning, or quantization.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Designs distributed model serving systems with auto-scaling, latency monitoring, and dynamic resource allocation.

criteria.name: Model Performance and Drift Monitoring
criteria.description: Ability to implement and maintain real-time monitoring for model performance and data drift.

scoring_levels.Level 0: No monitoring; unaware of data drift or performance degradation.
scoring_levels.Level 1: Uses basic logging; no automated alerts or performance tracking.
scoring_levels.Level 2: Implements basic drift detection (e.g., statistical tests); alerts on threshold breaches.
scoring_levels.Level 3: Uses automated tools (e.g., MLflow, Prometheus) to track model performance over time.
scoring_levels.Level 4: Proactively detects and alerts on concept drift; triggers retraining workflows automatically.
scoring_levels.Level 5: Builds a proactive drift detection system with anomaly detection and model retraining triggers.
